newsitem.title: DENMARK: Jyske posts bumper Q1,upholds expectations.
newsitem.headline: Jyske posts bumper Q1,upholds expectations.

text.p: Denmark's Jyske Bank posted bumper first quarter 1997 profits, buoyed by higher securities and foreign exchange results and lower losses and bad debt provisions and upheld earlier full year expectations.
The bank, Denmark's fourth biggest and the only one to release quarterly results, reported a 423 million crown ($65.2 million) profit before tax and extraordinary items for 1997's first three months.
This compared to analysts' average expectations of only 220 million crowns and a 225 million crowns result in the same 1996 period.
"Developments in 1997's first quarter have been generally positive with stable growth in core activities and satisfactory earnings," Jyske said in a statement accompanying its results.
Nonetheless the bank upheld earlier forecasts of a full year profit before tax, extraordinary items and securities in the 600-750 million range, compared to 1996's 657 million crowns.

Jyske also forecast core earnings before provisions for the whole year of between 950 million and 1.050 billion crowns, with loss and bad debt provisions estimated at 300-350 million crowns for the whole year.

Securities and foreign exchange results were dramatically better at 156 million crowns for the first quarter against 52 million crowns a year ago, while losses and bad debt provisions fell drastically to six million crowns from 79 million in 1996's first three months. --Ole Mikkelsen, Copenhagen newsroom +45-33969654 ($ = 6.486 Danish Crowns)
